name: Colorado

sales.rateNote: Colorado's 2.9% state rate is the lowest of any state with a sales tax, but cities, counties and special districts add their own taxes. Home-rule cities can run their own sales tax with their own rules, separately from the Department of Revenue.

local.levies: state-administered city, county and special district taxes (e.g. RTD, Scientific and Cultural Facilities District, Rural Transportation Authorities) plus self-collected taxes of home-rule cities, which set their own base and exemptions
local.capNote: State-administered local rate changes can take effect only on January 1 or July 1.

groceries.note: Food for home consumption (SNAP/WIC-eligible items, with Colorado exceptions such as candy and soft drinks) is exempt from the 2.9% state tax. Cities and counties may choose to tax food; RTD, CD and RTA district taxes follow the state treatment.

clothing.note: Clothing is taxable as tangible personal property; Colorado has no clothing exemption or sales tax holiday.

sales.holidayNote: Colorado has no sales tax holiday.

useTax.note: Consumer use tax is due at the state rate (plus applicable local use taxes) on taxable items bought without Colorado sales tax.

facts.text: Home-rule cities may administer their own sales tax, with their own licensing, rates and exemptions; the Department of Revenue does not collect those taxes.
Businesses can file and pay participating home-rule city taxes through the state's Sales & Use Tax System (SUTS).
Since January 1, 2026 (HB25B-1005), retailers can no longer keep the state sales tax vendor service fee; local service fees may still apply.
State-administered sales tax rate changes can only take effect on January 1 or July 1; the DR 1002 rate publication is updated on those dates.
Cities and counties that exempt food must use the state's definition, and all must exempt purchases paid with SNAP or WIC.
With the end of penny production in November 2025, the Department issued rounding guidance for retailers in March 2026.

property.levied: Local: counties, municipalities, school districts and special districts levy mills on assessed value; county assessors value property and county treasurers collect. The Division of Property Taxation (DOLA) oversees administration.

assessment.text: Taxable value = actual value x assessment rate. For 2026, residential property uses two rates: 7.05% for school district levies and 6.80% for other local government levies, the latter applied after a 10% reduction of the first $700,000 of actual value (minimum $1,000 assessed value). The school rate can be adjusted downward by the State Board of Equalization to respect the school revenue limit.

homestead.name: Senior Property Tax Exemption
homestead.text: Owners aged 65+ who have owned and lived in their home for at least 10 consecutive years before January 1 are exempt on 50% of the first $200,000 of actual value. There is no general homestead exemption for other owners.
homestead.applyBy: Apply to the county assessor between January 1 and July 15 (late filing until August 15 without appeal rights).

otherRelief.name: Senior primary residence classification
otherRelief.text: For 2025 and 2026, seniors who received the senior exemption in 2020 or later at a previous home can keep a comparable benefit on a new primary residence; SB26-116 ends this classification after tax year 2026.

otherRelief.name: Veterans with a disability and Gold Star spouses
otherRelief.text: Separate exemption program for veterans with a 100% permanent service-connected disability rating (or individual unemployability) who own and occupy their home on January 1, their surviving spouses, and Gold Star spouses.

facts.text: The 2026 residential assessment rate for school levies is 7.05%.
The 2026 residential rate for non-school local levies is 6.80%, after first reducing actual value by 10% on the first $700,000.
The senior exemption requires 10 consecutive years of ownership and occupancy before January 1 of the application year.
SB26-116 eliminates the qualified-senior primary residence classification after property tax year 2026.
From January 1, 2027, deadlines for the disabled veteran exemption align with the senior exemption deadlines.
